# Ferratum & GrowthBook | First Meeting
Date: 2026-09-22 | Duration: 29.200000762939453m

## Summary
Ferratum operates a fintech business with banking licenses in more than 15 countries, 600 microservices, and 200 engineers in Slovakia. The company uses GrowthBook 4.0.4 on-premises, originally adopting the community version mainly for feature flagging, and is considering an upgrade. It is reviewing prerequisites, scheduled features, SDK streaming, encrypted endpoints, and multi-project support. Visual experiments are not planned because of UX/UI capacity limits, although marketing is interested, and AI agent features are being explored, including a possible marketing approval workflow. Pricing combines a platform fee with user seats, while enterprise includes security features, support, and self-hosted or cloud-hosted options, including EU cloud hosting. Procurement is lengthy because of banking regulations and requires GDPR and ISO documentation. The budget follows an annual cycle, with a decision needed by September, and the target decision timeline is within one month. Marcel will send pricing and hosting options by October 7, while Martin will present them to IT leadership for budget approval, followed by possible IT feedback within two weeks.

## Keywords
feature flagging, on-premise licensing, pricing tiers, enterprise governance, fintech compliance, GrowthBook upgrade

# Ferratum & GrowthBook | Enterprise Commercial Status
Date: 2026-10-07 | Duration: 37m

## Summary
The discussion covered the shift from the Pro version to Community because the UX visual editor was used infrequently; 10 accounts operated until August 2024. Pro is available only through the cloud, while self-hosted deployments are limited to Enterprise or open source. Self-hosting was recommended for control and compliance, while cloud CDN costs vary with traffic, and SDK caching can reduce the impact of outages. DORA compliance requires resilience and independence, potentially supported by an internal proxy or CDN and load balancing for total availability. Cloud pricing includes a $40 base seat price, $10 per million requests, and $1 per GB of bandwidth, creating variable monthly costs. Concerns were raised about service shutdown after non-payment, including credit card expiration risk. An enterprise proposal with self-hosting, SSO, support, installments, and a fixed annual price below $40,000 was discussed. The client will provide traffic and bandwidth data, after which a proposal will support leadership’s decision on cost and compliance risks.

## Keywords
GrowthBook pricing, self-hosted version, Pro plan, CDN costs, DORA compliance, feature flagging
